Stock market corrections have a strange effect on investors. Prices fall a little, uncertainty rises a lot, and suddenly long-term investors start behaving like short-term traders.
But corrections are not an anomaly. They are part of the market’s natural rhythm. Almost every strong bull market in history has been punctuated by phases where prices cool off, valuations reset, and sentiment turns cautious. The real question is not whether corrections happen. The real question is how investors respond when they do.
